notes: NCI PDQ was reread at Communication Tools and Techniques — Ask-Tell-Ask. The first Ask elicits understanding/goals/values or permission; Tell gives the main message briefly without jargon; the second Ask checks whether the patient heard and absorbed the information and is ready to continue.
Official USMLE Content Outline (2026) page 39 was reread for patient interviewing, patient-centered communication, and information provision.

blueprint.system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

claim_audit.first_ask: Eliciting baseline understanding before explanation is part of the first Ask and permits tailoring.
claim_audit.tell: The Tell portion is brief, plain-language delivery of the main message rather than a comprehensive jargon-heavy lecture.
claim_audit.second_ask: The second Ask assesses how the information was received and readiness to proceed.
claim_audit.teach_back_distinction: The item tests the complete Ask-Tell-Ask conversational sequence rather than isolated teach-back as a health-literacy technique.
claim_audit.surrogate_distractor: No surrogate is indicated because the patient has capacity and has not delegated communication.
claim_audit.premature_choice_distractor: A treatment choice cannot be meaningfully elicited before relevant diagnostic information is provided.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Without using the staged key, the requested strategy must both start from the patient's existing understanding and explicitly reassess after a concise explanation. Only the Ask-Tell-Ask sequence does both.
adversarial_second_pass.teach_back_attack: The final Ask can check absorption, but the keyed response also includes the defining first Ask and Tell phases, making this a distinct full communication framework rather than a duplicate of a standalone teach-back item.
adversarial_second_pass.shared_decision_attack: Shared decision making is not yet the central task because the vignette concerns initial information exchange before treatment deliberation.
adversarial_second_pass.family_attack: Capacity and language concordance remove any indication for substitute family communication.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All choices are plausible communication approaches; the key is selected by the stated dual goals rather than length or wording.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No claim is made that Ask-Tell-Ask is superior in all contexts or that a specific number of information chunks is required.
